Not by default. December 22nd falls inside the year-end code freeze (Dec 15 to Jan 5), while Finance runs the annual close. No production release may go out in that window, and that includes hotfixes.

**What would let it go out:** a lead in #fin-eng has to sign off in the channel before the release. If Finance is the one asking for the fix, they may be able to get that sign-off quickly.

**The rest of the process, if you get sign-off:**
- December 22nd is a Tuesday, so the "no Fridays after 14:00 UTC" rule doesn't apply.
- Tag from `main` as `vYYYY.MM.N`, here something like `v2026.12.1`. CI builds and publishes, and you never publish by hand.
- The release checklist in the PR template must be complete first.
- It promotes to staging automatically. Production then needs a manual approval in the CI UI from someone on the billing team, so line up that person ahead of time.
- Any database migrations the fix needs must ship in the same release.

**Alternative:** if the fix isn't urgent enough to justify an exception, release before December 15th. That avoids the freeze entirely, and you have plenty of time since today is October 4th.

I can help get the fix ready for an earlier release, or draft the #fin-eng sign-off request.
